profile.summary: This is the evaluation published with OncoVI, a Python tool that automates the ClinGen, CGC and VICC oncogenicity guidelines for somatic variants. OncoVI's classifications are compared against four reference sets: 93 variants supplied by the guideline authors, 7,802 real-world variants from the Erlangen Molecular Tumor Board, 691 ClinVar variants with curated oncogenicity classifications, and a 135-variant subset of the tumour board variants that three expert cancer biologists reclassified under the guidelines. Every comparison is a three-class agreement rate between OncoVI and the reference. It shows how far an automated reading of the guidelines matches guideline authors, a tumour board and ClinVar.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Materials and Methods, the four data set sections; Results

summary_quotes.text: To harmonize and automate oncogenicity classification, Oncogenicity Variant Interpreter (OncoVI), an open-source, Python-based implementation of the Clinical Genome Resource/Cancer Genomics Consortium/Variant Interpretation for Cancer Consortium oncogenicity guidelines, was developed.
OncoVI achieved an accuracy of 80% on a gold standard set of 93 somatic variants provided by the guidelines, with a sensitivity of 88% for oncogenic/likely oncogenic variants.

When applied to a real-world set of 7802 variants from 557 participants previously evaluated by the Molecular Tumor Board (MTB) Erlangen, OncoVI showed 79% concordance with the prior MTB assessment of variant impact on protein function.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether software can apply the oncogenicity guidelines and reach the same class a human assessor would. For each variant OncoVI collects evidence from public resources, decides which of the 11 oncogenic and five benign criteria are triggered, sums their points and maps the total to a class: 10 or more is oncogenic, 6 to 9 likely oncogenic, 0 to 5 a variant of uncertain significance, minus 1 to minus 6 likely benign, and minus 7 or lower benign. The comparisons then ask how often that class matches the guideline authors' own classification, a tumour board's assessment of protein function, ClinVar's curated oncogenicity call, and a blinded expert reclassification under the same guidelines.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Four sets, each with a different reference. The standard operating procedure set is 93 variants taken from Supplementary Tables 1 and 3 of the guideline paper, with the triggered criteria, scores and classifications as the authors published them; genomic coordinates for 23 of them had to be derived by hand from the DNA change. The tumour board set is 7,802 unique somatic variants across 489 genes from 557 people seen by the Comprehensive Cancer Center Erlangen-EMN tumour board between February 2022 and February 2024, sequenced from formalin-fixed tissue with the TruSight Oncology 500 assay and classified into five classes by three expert cancer biologists. The ClinVar set is the 691 somatic variants, out of 6,113, that had an NCBI-curated oncogenicity classification as of 12 April 2025. The validation set is 135 tumour board variants chosen after the fact from the confusion matrix, taking every strong disagreement plus random variants from selected cells, which the same three experts then reclassified under the guidelines while blinded to how OncoVI implements the criteria.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Variants are annotated by a Python pipeline built on Ensembl VEP version 111.0 against GRCh38, with the dbNSFP 4.5a and SpliceAI plugins, keeping only coding consequences, dropping variants with a global gnomAD frequency of 0.025 or more, and preferring the MANE canonical transcript. OncoVI then queries the knowledgebases behind each criterion and produces a class. For scoring, the five classes are collapsed to three (oncogenic or likely oncogenic, uncertain, benign or likely benign) and compared with the reference as accuracy or concordance, with per-class sensitivity, confusion matrices, and stratification by gene class and by functional consequence. Scores assigned by OncoVI and by the reference are compared by correlation on the variants where the classes agree.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, Variant Annotation via the VEP-Based In-House Pipeline and Data Analysis and Statistical Analysis; Results

quotes.text: the variants are functionally annotated with the VEP from Ensembl (VEP version 111.0, January 2024) using GRCh38 and Reference Sequence Database<xref rid="bib35" ref-type="bibr"><sup>35</sup></xref> as preferred cache
Two VEP plugins, dbNSFP version 4.5a and spliceAI, were used to retrieve scores from predictive algorithms.
the filter_vep tool removed from the VCF the variants without consequence and/or with a global gnomAD population frequency ≥0.025
the canonical transcript according to the Matched Annotation from NCBI and EBI (MANE) project<xref rid="bib36" ref-type="bibr"><sup>36</sup></xref> was favored
To evaluate OncoVI performance, variants were grouped into O/LO, B/LB, and VUS classes.
Spearman correlations were computed using cor.test() from the stats package.

sections.title: Reported results
sections.body: On the guideline authors' 93 variants OncoVI reached 81% accuracy (75 of 93), with sensitivity 88% (38 of 43) for oncogenic or likely oncogenic and 83% (10 of 12) for benign or likely benign, and the scores correlated with the guideline authors' at r = 0.87. On the 7,802 tumour board variants the three-class concordance was 78% (6,060 of 7,802), which breaks down as 97% for uncertain variants (3,955 of 4,092) but 43% for benign or likely benign (961 of 2,261). On the 691 ClinVar variants it was 83% (573 of 691), with sensitivity 84% (362 of 431) for oncogenic or likely oncogenic and no variant crossing between the oncogenic and benign extremes. The validation set is the striking one: the experts' guideline-based reclassification agreed with the earlier tumour board assessment for only 34% of the 135 variants (46 of 135), and OncoVI agreed with the tumour board on 22% (30 of 135) but with the experts' reclassification on 80% (108 of 135).
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, Performance on the SOP, MTB and ClinVar data sets and Comparative Analysis with Expert Re-Assessment

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: OncoVI is distributed as a repository with a conda setup, a resource preparation script, a VEP installation path and an example input. It supports GRCh38 only, takes variants as text or VCF, and writes a tab-delimited Excel file holding the annotation fields, the variant-specific score, the classification and the triggered criteria. The repository also ships OncoVI_mod, a version that avoids the licensed OncoKB resource by defining oncogene and tumour suppressor roles from COSMIC instead.
sections.source_locator: Repository: README.md, Get started, Test OncoVI on an exemplary set of variants and OncoVI_mod. Paper: Results

quotes.text: OncoVI supports only variants in human genome assembly GRCh38. No other genome assemblies are currently supported.
Variants in both text format and in variant call format (VCF) are accepted by OncoVI. No other formats are currently supported.
The current output format produced by OncoVI is a tab-delimited excel file.
In OncoVI_mod, the role of tumour suppressor genes and oncogenes is defined using COSMIC only and the other resources available to OncoVI.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: Four. SOP set: 93 somatic variants from the guideline authors, classified by them as 14 oncogenic, 29 likely oncogenic, 38 uncertain, 6 likely benign and 6 benign. Molecular Tumor Board set: 7,802 unique somatic variants across 489 genes from 557 individuals. ClinVar set: 691 somatic variants across 227 genes with an NCBI oncogenicity classification, out of 6,113 candidates, comprising 1 benign, 1 likely benign, 373 likely oncogenic, 58 oncogenic and 258 uncertain. Validation set: 135 tumour board variants across 104 genes, reclassified by three experts.

quotes.text: SOP oncogenicity classification had assigned the variants to five classes as follows: oncogenic: 14, likely oncogenic: 29, VUS: 38, likely benign: 6, and benign: 6 (<xref rid="appsec1" ref-type="sec">Supplemental Table S1</xref>).
comprises 7802 unique somatic variants across 489 genes, identified in a cohort of 557 individuals

These 135 variants involved 104 different genes (67 OGs, 61 TSGs, and 7 with an unknown role), and were mainly truncating (<italic toggle="yes">n</italic> = 63), missense (<italic toggle="yes">n</italic> = 50), or splice site variants.

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: None in the machine learning sense: OncoVI is a rule implementation, so every variant in every set is scored and compared, with no training or held-out portion. The only derived subset is the 135-variant validation set, which was selected after the fact from the tumour board confusion matrix: all variants with the strongest disagreement plus randomly chosen variants from the cells where OncoVI said uncertain or oncogenic.

quotes.text: the validation data set was generated on the basis of the obtained confusion matrix between MTB and OncoVI classifications by considering: all the variants with the strongest disagreement
randomly chosen variants from the confusion matrix cells corresponding to OncoVI classification as VUS and O/LO, with a higher number from the MTB P/LP variants classified as VUS by OncoVI

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Three-class agreement, higher better: accuracy or concordance between OncoVI's class and the reference's, reported as a percentage with the counts, plus per-class sensitivity and a confusion matrix. Correlation between OncoVI's variant-specific score and the reference's score is reported for the variants where the classes agree. Agreement is also stratified by gene class (oncogene against tumour suppressor) and by functional consequence.

quotes.text: To evaluate OncoVI performance, variants were grouped into O/LO, B/LB, and VUS classes.
Confusion matrix of the agreement between the SOP and OncoVI in classifying the variants of the SOP data set.

When evaluating the performance stratified by gene classes (OGs versus TSGs), differently from the SOP data set, higher concordance for variants in OGs compared with TSGs was observed (82.5% versus 76.0%)
the performance stratified by functional consequence showed higher concordance for missense variants compared with truncating alterations (78.2% versus 49.4%)

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: No other software is compared. The reference points are human: the guideline authors' own published classifications, the tumour board's five-class assessment of protein function, ClinVar's NCBI-curated oncogenicity classification, and three expert cancer biologists reclassifying under the guidelines. The repository adds an internal comparison between OncoVI and OncoVI_mod, which drops the licensed OncoKB resource, reported in a separate document rather than in the paper.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Blinding on the one comparison where it applies: the three experts reclassified the 135 validation variants while blinded to how OncoVI implements the criteria, although they were given the list of resources OncoVI uses for each criterion and had themselves produced the original tumour board classification. For the other three sets no control applies, because OncoVI is a rule implementation with no training data. The criteria were, however, interpreted by the OncoVI authors where the guideline text was unclear, and resources were chosen by them where the guidelines suggested none.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, Validation Data Set; Results

quotes.text: while remaining blinded to OncoVI implementation of the criteria
each expert was provided with the list of the resources used by OncoVI for each criterion
Each criterion was interpreted whenever its biological meaning resulted unclear from the SOP textual indication.

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: No intervals on the agreement rates. The paper reports counts behind every percentage, correlation coefficients with p values for the score comparisons, and Fisher exact tests for the association between triggered criteria and correct classification, with significance at p of 0.05 or below. There are no replicates: the classifications are deterministic given the resources, and resource versions are pinned in the methods rather than varied.

The pipeline performs demultiplexing, FASTQ generation, DNA/RNA alignment to the human reference genome (University of California, Santa Cruz, hg19), and calling of single and multiple nucleotide variants, copy number variants, fusions, and splice variants.

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Genomic coordinates on GRCh38, as a text table or a VCF, and whatever the integrated public resources return for them. The pipeline uses VEP annotation with dbNSFP and SpliceAI scores, gnomAD frequencies, ClinVar, COSMIC and, in the default configuration, the licensed OncoKB; no sequence model or structure is involved.

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: None. OncoVI is a deterministic rule engine: each criterion is coded as IF-ELSE logic over the resources, points are summed and the class follows from fixed thresholds. Nothing is trained, fitted or tuned on any of the four reference sets.

steps.source_locator: Repository: README.md, Instructions to set up VEP manually. Paper: Materials and Methods, Variant Annotation via the VEP-Based In-House Pipeline

quotes.text: conda install bioconda::ensembl-vep
Two VEP plugins, dbNSFP version 4.5a and spliceAI, were used to retrieve scores from predictive algorithms.

steps.title: Run OncoVI on the example variants
steps.explanation: The README's own run command, with its cd step. The example input is the guideline authors' variant table, which is the SOP data set used in the paper.
steps.source_locator: Repository: README.md, Test OncoVI on an exemplary set of variants

quotes.text: python 02_VEP_based_pipeline.py -i ../testdata/SOP_table_union.txt
# ~/oncovi/testdata/SOP_table_union.txt

outputs: A tab-delimited Excel file of the variants that passed annotation and classification, holding the VEP and ClinVar annotation fields, the variant-specific score (Points), the oncogenicity classification (Classification) and the triggered criteria (Criteria). An example output is included in the repository.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The resource preparation script and the VEP cache and plugin downloads need site-specific paths, so the steps here stop short of reproducing the paper's results end to end.
No published command computes the agreement rates in the paper; OncoVI produces classifications and the comparisons were done separately in R.
The default configuration depends on the licensed OncoKB resource; the repository's OncoVI_mod avoids it but gives different oncogene and tumour suppressor assignments.

structured.task: OncoVI three-class assessment: ClinVar April 2025 oncogenicity assertions
structured.dataset: ClinVar somatic variants with an NCBI oncogenicity classification, accessed 12 April 2025
structured.split: no split, all variants with an available oncogenicity classification

quotes.text: The ClinVar data set includes 691 somatic variants with available oncogenicity classification in ClinVar (<ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/tab_delimited" id="intref0080"><italic toggle="yes">https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/tab_delimited</italic></ext-link>, variant_summary.txt.gz, last accessed April 12, 2025<italic toggle="yes">).

involving 227 genes

structured.task: OncoVI three-class assessment: MTB selected expert reassessment
structured.dataset: validation data set of MTB variants reclassified by three experts under the oncogenicity guidelines
structured.split: selected a posteriori from the MTB confusion matrix, enriched for disagreements
structured.primary_metric: agreement with the experts' guideline-based reclassification

quotes.text: The validation data set of 135 somatic variants was generated from the MTB data set to validate the implementation of the oncogenicity criteria in OncoVI.
the agreement with experts' re-assessment reached 80% (<italic toggle="yes">n</italic> = 108/135) (<xref rid="fig4" ref-type="fig">Figure 4</xref>B)
These 135 variants involved 104 different genes (67 OGs, 61 TSGs, and 7 with an unknown role)
The MIT license file applies to only the scripts within this repository.

notes: Written from the PMC full text (PMC13269341, CC BY) and the MGCarta/oncovi README at commit 75d56d0175544cd4732b63a4c69cf46b1b1aeb23. Points for a human. First, the abstract says 80% accuracy on the 93-variant SOP set while the Results section says 81% (75 of 93); both are recorded as printed and the structured entry uses the Results figure. Second, the abstract says 79% concordance on the tumour board set while the Results section says 78% (6,060 of 7,802); the same applies. Third, the validation set's 80% agreement is against the experts' reclassification, not against the original tumour board assessment, which OncoVI matched on 22% of the same 135 variants; the two must not be mixed. Fourth, the variant counts here are per data set as the methods and results print them, and the data sets overlap: the 135 validation variants are a subset of the 7,802. Fifth, no data are released for the tumour board cohort, so data_licence is null; code_licence is MIT because the README states that the MIT licence applies to the repository's scripts.
